mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell?
options: The salt bridge carries electrons between the two electrodes.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
It completes the circuit by allowing ions to flow between the half-cells, maintaining electrical neutrality.
Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH 0.

mcqs.q: When an acid neutralises an alkali, what is the pH of the resulting solution?
options: Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH exactly 7 regardless of the acid and base used.
Approximately 7 if equivalent amounts of strong acid and strong alkali react — but it varies with strength.
Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH 0.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: 0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
